text: Was reading about him and some great stories apart from the 2+2=5 one

During the 1959 Candidates Tournament, Tal found himself staring at a position against Nezhmetdinov. Instead of calculating, he began thinking about a children's poem by Korney Chukovsky about a hippopotamus stuck in a marsh. He spent 20 minutes wondering how one would actually drag a hippo out of a swamp before suddenly making a knight sacrifice. When asked about the move later, he admitted the hippo had helped him stop over-calculating and just trust his intuition.
For those who haven’t heard “take your opponent in the deep forest where 2+2=5, and path for outside is only wide enough for one”

And this one
In 1988, long after his prime and with his health failing, a 51-year-old Tal entered the first official World Blitz Championship. The field included the legendary Garry Kasparov and Anatoly Karpov. To everyone's shock, the "Magician" conjured one last miracle, finishing ahead of both titans to take the gold medal
